judged_text: In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the Hubspot caller types and uses the result as HubspotToken (a parsed token object with accessToken/expiresIn), so downstream property reads get undefined. With credential sharing enabled, expiry is computed from hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn === undefined, producing NaN/expired expiry dates and tokens read as undefined, corrupting the stored Hubspot credential and failing all subsequent Hubspot API calls.

With credential sharing enabled, expiry is computed from hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn === undefined, producing NaN/expired expiry dates and tokens read as undefined, corrupting the stored Hubspot credential and failing all subsequent Hubspot API calls.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential-sharing mode is active (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), the function returns the raw `fetch(...)` result (a `Response`). In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the caller assigns `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` where the non-sync path returns a HubSpot SDK token object, but the sync path will instead return a `Response`. This is a concrete runtime type/shape mismatch introduced by the diff and will cause downstream reads like `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` / `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` (or similar) to be `undefined` when sync mode is enabled.
